verdict.rationale: ROS 2 has machine-readable interface definitions. Client libraries are built from code generators, and the community describes shared message packages as being like a collection of .proto files, which is an IDL roughly equivalent to an API spec. The evidence never shows a first-party, downloadable OpenAPI-style spec of the ROS 2 API, and the IDL point rests mainly on a community analogy. Missing for 10: first-party docs describing the interface definition format (msg/srv/action) as a downloadable spec, a machine-readable spec of the ROS 2 graph or CLI APIs, OpenAPI or equivalent export tooling, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can download a machine-readable API spec (OpenAPI or equivalent)

citations.quote: all client libraries implement code generators
like a big collection of .proto files for complex robotics datatypes that everyone agrees to use
